name: Safety Technology
title: Safety Technology
answer: Safety technology in schools includes AI security products such as camera analytics and weapon detection. The book warns that the research gathered for this Volume found no independent evaluation of these systems in schools, so districts should ask vendors for independent evidence and treat safety claims like savings claims. This matters because physical safety depends mostly on people and procedures, and technology can support but not replace them.

sections.body: Some vendors sell AI systems for school security, including camera analytics and weapon detection. These products can be expensive and are often marketed with strong claims. The research gathered for this Volume found no independent evaluation of these systems in schools. The idea is to approach safety technology with caution, asking vendors for independent evidence and applying the savings claim questions in this chapter to safety claims too. It solves the problem of districts possibly buying costly tools without proof they work, while privacy and fairness risks remain.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text does not give grade bands for this idea. Districts considering these systems should ask vendors for independent evidence and apply the savings claim questions from this chapter to safety claims. Any alert from a security system should be reviewed by trained staff before action is taken. Physical safety depends mostly on trained staff, clear procedures, good relationships with students, and regular drills. Technology can support these things, but it cannot replace them.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book's evidence label is that the research gathered for this Volume found no independent evaluation of these systems in schools. It does not cite a study, figure, or finding beyond that absence. The text also says these products are often marketed with strong claims, which is why districts should ask for independent evidence. So the evidence base for safety technology in schools is not established by independent evaluation in the text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Security systems raise the same privacy and fairness questions as the monitoring tools in Chapter 15. Cameras that analyze behavior or identify people collect sensitive information about students and visitors. False alarms can cause fear, disruption, and wrongful suspicion. Any alert should be reviewed by trained staff before action is taken. Boards should be wary of spending on technology at the expense of people, because physical safety depends mostly on people and procedures.
